intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this tour offers breathtaking aerial views of the forest and chances to spot toucans, howler monkeys, and resplendent quetzals along the way.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. Between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges Nature Walk
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of hanging bridges suspended high above the forest floor near the iconic Arenal Volcano. This self-guided or guided eco-walk offers stunning volcano views and excellent wildlife spotting opportunities including poison dart frogs, coatis, and exotic birds.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Explore one of Costa Rica's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide armed with a high-powered spotting scope. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and basilisk lizards, then cool off on the park's pristine white-sand beaches after the hike.

experiences.name: Traditional Costa Rican Cooking Class & Farm Visit
experiences.description: Visit a local family-run finca (farm) to learn how to prepare authentic Costa Rican dishes including gallo pinto, casado, and fresh ceviche using ingredients harvested directly from the garden. Gain insight into the Pura Vida food culture, enjoy a communal meal, and take home handwritten recipes as a souvenir.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives late evening
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange shared shuttle or public bus transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (budget tip: shared shuttles cost ~$10-15 vs $60+ for private taxi). Check in and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport if hungry — look for the Musmanni bakery or Subway inside the terminal for budget-friendly options under $8

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. Have local colones or USD ready for tips and small purchases. Exchange a small amount at the airport kiosk if needed. Rest well — adventures begin tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a morning stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings. Watch for shorebirds, pelicans, and possibly scarlet macaws in the surrounding trees — a free wildlife experience right at your doorstep.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest local town on foot or by public bus. Visit the local mercado (market) to sample fresh tropical fruits like maracuyá, guanábana, and cas. Pick up a detailed map and chat with locals about free or low-cost spots nearby. Visit any nearby public beach for a swim and relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a casual sunset walk along the beach. Look for bioluminescent plankton in the surf after dark — a magical free natural phenomenon common on Costa Rica's coasts in February.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the resort if breakfast is included, or find a local soda (small family restaurant) nearby for a classic Gallo Pinto (rice and beans with egg) for ~$3-4
meals.lunch: Local soda lunch — casado plate (rice, beans, salad, protein) for ~$5-7
meals.dinner: Self-cater with fresh fruit and bread from the market, or try a local soda for ~$6-8. Look for 'menu del día' specials

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is an orientation day. Keep spending low. Pick up a SIM card at a local shop (Kolbi or Claro) for ~$10-15 with data for navigation throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along a nearby nature trail or beach. February is dry season on many parts of Costa Rica's Pacific coast — expect sunny skies and excellent wildlife visibility. Look for howler monkeys, iguanas, coatis, and tropical birds. Bring binoculars if you have them.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a budget zip-lining experience through a local operator near your resort area. Many areas offer zip-line tours for $35-55 per person — book directly with local operators rather than through hotel desks to save 20-30%. Enjoy the canopy views and adrenaline rush over the rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and freshen up. Head out for a budget seafood dinner at a local beachside restaurant. Watch for crabs and small creatures on the beach after dark.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto at a local soda ~$3-4
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from the market — fruit, bread, and local cheese ~$3-5 — eat at the zip-line or trailhead
meals.dinner: Fresh fish or shrimp at a local beachside soda ~$8-12. Ask for the catch of the day (pescado del día)

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining the day before if possible to secure your spot and negotiate pricing. Always confirm what safety equipment is included. Wear closed-toe shoes and light layers for the canopy.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided or self-guided mangrove kayak tour if available near your resort area. Mangroves are incredible wildlife corridors — spot herons, kingfishers, crocodiles, and monkeys. Many operators offer 2-3 hour tours for $25-40. Alternatively, rent a kayak independently for ~$10-15/hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife refuge. Costa Rica's national parks charge a modest entrance fee (~$18 for foreigners) which directly funds conservation. Spend the afternoon hiking well-marked trails and observing wildlife in their natural habitat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to base and enjoy a quiet evening. Try cooking a simple meal using local ingredients from the market — plantains, rice, beans, and eggs are cheap and nutritious. Enjoy the sounds of the tropical night from your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit plate and coffee at a local soda ~$4-5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or quick roadside empanadas ~$2-4
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal with market ingredients ~$4-6, or local soda casado ~$6-8

day_by_day.notes: Bring insect repellent (DEET-based) and sunscreen for outdoor activities. Stay hydrated — carry a reusable water bottle and refill at your accommodation. February temperatures can reach 30°C+ in the Pacific lowlands.

day_by_day.morning: Arrange an early morning bird-watching walk. Costa Rica has over 900 bird species — February is an excellent time to spot both resident and migratory birds. Hire a local birding guide for ~$20-30 for a 2-3 hour walk, or use a free birding app like Merlin Bird ID and self-guide along a nature trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local waterfall if one is accessible from your area. Many stunning waterfalls in Costa Rica are reachable by public bus and short hike with little to no entrance fee. Cool off with a swim in the natural pool beneath the falls.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local farmers' market (feria) if one operates nearby in the evening or check for a weekly evening market. Sample local street food — chorreadas (corn pancakes), tamales, and fresh coconut water are affordable and delicious.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before bird walk — granola bar and banana ~$1-2
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch near the waterfall — bread, local cheese, fruit ~$4-5
meals.dinner: Street food at the evening market ~$5-8

day_by_day.notes: For the waterfall visit, wear water shoes or sandals with good grip. Don't leave valuables unattended at swimming holes. Check with locals about current water levels and trail conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby wildlife rescue center or sanctuary. Many operate on donation-based or low-cost entry (~$15-20) and house sloths, monkeys, toucans, and other rescued animals. This is an ethical and educational wildlife experience that directly supports conservation.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the sanctuary, explore a nearby town's central plaza and church. Sit in the park and people-watch — a quintessential Costa Rican experience. Browse local artisan stalls for affordable handmade souvenirs like painted ox-cart miniatures, seed jewelry, or woven goods.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event if available — check local bulletin boards for community events, live music, or football matches. Enjoy a cold Imperial or Pilsen beer (Costa Rica's local lagers) at a local bar ~$1.50-2 each.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or soda breakfast ~$3-5
meals.lunch: Soda near the wildlife center ~$5-7
meals.dinner: Local pizza or pasta restaurant for variety ~$8-10, or traditional soda for less

day_by_day.notes: When visiting wildlife sanctuaries, choose centers that do not allow selfies with wild animals or encourage handling — these are signs of ethical operations. Your entry fee supports animal rehabilitation and release programs.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip rest and recharge day. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend the morning relaxing on your beachfront. Practice snorkeling if gear is available to rent (~$5-10/day) and explore the underwater world just offshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Organize and review photos, update a travel journal, and plan the second half of your trip. Take a long walk along the beach collecting shells and watching wildlife. Look for hermit crabs, ghost crabs, and shorebirds along the tideline.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate the halfway point of your trip. Find a restaurant with fresh ceviche — a Costa Rican coastal staple — and enjoy a full sit-down meal with a view of the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — treat yourself ~$6-8
meals.lunch: Light beach snack — coconut water and fresh fruit from a beach vendor ~$3-5
meals.dinner: Slightly elevated dinner with fresh ceviche, grilled fish, and a local beer ~$15-20 — a worthy mid-trip splurge

day_by_day.notes: Use this rest day to do laundry (many budget accommodations have laundry facilities or nearby laundromats for ~$5-8 per load), recharge devices, and reorganize your pack for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Arrange a guided horseback riding tour through the rainforest or along the beach. Many local farms offer 2-3 hour rides for $35-50 per person — a fun and authentic way to explore the landscape while supporting local families. Spot wildlife from a higher vantage point.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local cacao or coffee plantation for a farm tour. Costa Rica is world-renowned for its coffee and chocolate. Small-scale farm tours run $15-25 and include tastings — learn about the process from bean to cup or pod to bar. Purchase local coffee or chocolate as budget-friendly souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a group meal at your accommodation using local ingredients, or organize a potluck with other travelers staying at the resort. Share stories and travel tips — fellow budget travelers are often the best source of local knowledge.

meals.breakfast: Early soda breakfast before horseback ride ~$4-6
meals.lunch: Lunch included with plantation tour, or nearby soda ~$5-7
meals.dinner: Self-catered or communal meal ~$4-6 per person

day_by_day.notes: When booking horseback riding, ask about the condition of the horses and choose operators who demonstrate animal welfare. A well-fed, healthy horse with proper tack is a sign of a responsible operator.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longer zip-line or canopy tour if your area offers multi-line circuits (10-15 platforms) for a more immersive experience. Some operators also offer Tarzan swings, rappelling, and hanging bridges as add-ons — negotiate a package deal for better value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby river for white-water tubing or gentle river floating — a budget-friendly alternative to full rafting tours (~$20-30 for tubing vs $70-90 for guided rafting). Enjoy the jungle scenery from the water and watch for river wildlife including basilisk lizards and kingfishers.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening at a local bar or restaurant with live music. Many coastal towns in Costa Rica have weekly live music nights featuring marimba, salsa, or reggaeton. Enjoy the local nightlife without overspending.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fresh juice and toast at a café ~$4-6
meals.lunch: Riverside soda or packed lunch ~$4-6
meals.dinner: Bar snacks and local beer while enjoying live music ~$8-12

day_by_day.notes: River activities are generally safe in February (dry season means lower, clearer water levels), but always follow guide instructions and wear provided life jackets. Store electronics in waterproof bags.

day_by_day.morning: Take a public bus or shared shuttle to a nearby protected area or biological reserve for a full-day eco-adventure. Costa Rica's extensive protected area network means world-class nature is always within reach. Arrive early for the best wildlife sightings — animals are most active in the first two hours after dawn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the reserve or protected area. Look for sloths hanging in cecropia trees, poison dart frogs on the forest floor, and toucans and parrots in the canopy. Take your time on the trails — slow and quiet movement yields the best wildlife encounters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Enjoy a quiet evening walk on the beach as the sun sets — February sunsets on Costa Rica's Pacific coast are spectacular. Watch for sea turtle tracks on the beach (February is nesting season for some species).

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast before departure ~$3-5 at a soda
meals.lunch: Packed lunch brought from the market — sandwiches, fruit, nuts ~$4-6
meals.dinner: Hearty casado at a local soda after a long day ~$6-8

day_by_day.notes: Wear neutral-colored clothing (avoid bright colors and strong perfumes) for wildlife watching. Bring a small daypack with water (2L minimum), snacks, rain jacket, and a first aid kit. Stay on marked trails.

day_by_day.morning: Take a sunrise yoga or meditation session on the beach — many resorts and local studios offer free or donation-based morning sessions. The beachfront setting at Aegean Bliss Resort makes this a perfect way to connect with the natural environment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on a DIY eco-adventure: rent a bicycle ($5-10/day) and explore the surrounding countryside. Visit a local village, chat with residents, and discover hidden gems that tour operators don't cover. Look for roadside fruit stands selling fresh pipa fría (cold green coconut) for ~$1.
day_by_day.evening: Arrange a guided night walk with a local naturalist guide (~$20-30 per person). Night walks reveal a completely different world — tree frogs, sleeping birds, insects, bats, and nocturnal mammals like kinkajous and armadillos. A headlamp is essential.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga snack — banana and coffee ~$2-3, then full breakfast after ~$4-5
meals.lunch: Roadside fruit and snacks during cycling ~$3-5
meals.dinner: Early dinner before night walk — local soda casado ~$6-8

day_by_day.notes: For the night walk, wear long pants and closed shoes to protect against insects and vegetation. Bring insect repellent. Keep voices low and follow your guide's instructions for the best wildlife encounters.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a final signature eco-adventure activity — choose based on what you haven't done yet: stand-up paddleboarding on calm coastal waters (~$15-20/hour), a boat tour to spot dolphins and sea turtles (~$35-50), or a guided snorkeling trip to a nearby reef (~$25-40).
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin souvenir shopping and gift purchasing at local markets and artisan shops. Budget-friendly authentic souvenirs include: locally grown coffee ($5-10/bag), handmade jewelry ($3-15), mini painted ox-carts ($5-10), and locally made hot sauce ($3-5). Avoid airport shops where prices are 2-3x higher.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant discovered during the trip. Reflect on your 13-day eco-adventure over a delicious meal. If budget allows, order a special Costa Rican dessert like tres leches cake or arroz con leche.

meals.breakfast: Favorite breakfast spot from the trip ~$4-6
meals.lunch: Light lunch to save room for farewell dinner ~$4-6
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — slightly elevated budget treat ~$15-25 with drinks

day_by_day.notes: Pack souvenirs carefully — wrap fragile items in clothing. Check airline regulations for bringing food items home (coffee and sealed chocolate are generally fine; fresh fruit is not). Keep receipts for customs declarations.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise walk on the beachfront. Take photos, collect final memories, and say goodbye to the ocean. Pack remaining belongings and do a thorough room check for forgotten items — chargers, toiletries, and documents are commonly left behind.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrange your pre-booked shared shuttle or public bus transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport. Allow at least 3-4 hours before your flight for travel and check-in, as Costa Rican roads can be slow. If time permits before departure, grab a final coffee and snack at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Board your return flight. Carry snacks from the market to avoid expensive airport food. Reflect on an incredible 13 days of eco-adventure, zip-lining, wildlife encounters, and budget-savvy travel through one of the world's most biodiverse countries.

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto breakfast at a local soda near the resort ~$3-5
meals.lunch: Airport food or snacks packed from the market ~$5-10
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: BUDGET SUMMARY TIPS: Total estimated daily budget ~$50-70/day excluding accommodation (meals ~$15-20, activities ~$20-35, transport ~$5-10, miscellaneous ~$5-10). Book activities directly with local operators to save 20-30%. Use public buses whenever possible (~$1-3 per trip vs $15-40 for shuttles). Eat at sodas (local family restaurants) for authentic, affordable meals. Pura Vida!

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged private transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light snack from the resort's 24-hour room service or a small convenience store near the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid stress upon late-night arrival. Confirm check-in details with Aegean Bliss Resort ahead of time. Keep the first night simple – rest is the priority after a long travel day.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow orientation walk along the beachfront to get your bearings, feel the Pacific breeze, and acclimate to Costa Rica's tropical climate. Explore the resort grounds and pool area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest town for a casual exploration of local shops, sodas (small local eateries), and the beachside promenade. Visit a local market if available to pick up snacks, sunscreen, and essentials. Enjoy a relaxed swim at the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the beach terrace at the resort, followed by a welcome dinner at a well-regarded local seafood restaurant near the resort. Enjoy fresh ceviche and grilled fish while soaking in the coastal ambiance.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – enjoy fresh tropical fruits, gallo pinto (rice and beans), eggs, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a nearby soda – try a casado (traditional plate with rice, beans, salad, and protein) for around $8–12 USD
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at a mid-range beachfront restaurant – budget $20–30 USD per person. Try fresh sea bass (corvina) or shrimp in garlic sauce

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to recover from jet lag. Stay hydrated, apply sunscreen generously – the Costa Rican sun is intense even on cloudy days. Exchange some USD to Costa Rican Colones at a local bank or ATM for small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike – Depart early (7:00 AM) to beat the crowds and heat. A certified naturalist guide will lead you through one of Costa Rica's most biodiverse national parks. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, sloths, scarlet macaws, coatis, and possibly a rare squirrel monkey. The guide's spotting scope and expertise make all the difference.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, relax on the stunning white-sand beaches within Manuel Antonio National Park – some of the most beautiful in the country. Swim in the calm coves, snorkel if conditions allow, and enjoy the rare experience of monkeys walking along the beach beside you.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy dinner at a local restaurant in the Manuel Antonio village strip, known for its excellent dining scene with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure – gallo pinto, eggs, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks brought from the resort, or purchase food from vendors near the park entrance (budget $8–15 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Manuel Antonio village – try La Luna or a similar spot. Budget $20–30 USD per person. Recommended: fresh tuna, plantains, and a local Imperial beer

day_by_day.notes: Book the guided wildlife hike in advance. Wear light, breathable clothing and sturdy walking shoes. Bring insect repellent, sunscreen, binoculars if you have them, and a reusable water bottle. The park has a daily visitor cap, so entry tickets must be purchased online ahead of time.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Costa Rican Cooking Class & Farm Visit – Visit a local family-run finca (farm) for an immersive half-day cooking experience. Learn how to make authentic Costa Rican staples including gallo pinto, plantain dishes, arroz con leche, and fresh tortillas. Tour the farm's garden of tropical fruits, herbs, and spices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort after the cooking class (which usually wraps up with a shared meal). Spend the afternoon at leisure – lounge by the pool, enjoy a beachside massage at the resort spa, or take a kayak or paddleboard rental along the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Casual evening at the resort bar. Enjoy a sunset caipirinha or fresh fruit smoothie. Dine at the resort's on-site restaurant, which should offer a solid mid-range menu featuring local and international dishes.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: The cooking class typically concludes with eating the dishes you prepared – this serves as your lunch (usually included in the tour price)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's restaurant – budget $18–25 USD per person. Try the catch of the day or a local stew

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is a wonderful cultural immersion activity and a great mid-trip break from adventure activities. Confirm whether the farm visit is included in the experience price. Bring a small notebook to jot down recipes to recreate at home.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart early for the drive/shuttle to Arenal Volcano region (approximately 4–5 hours from the Manuel Antonio/Pacific coast area). Enjoy the scenic route through Costa Rica's central highlands, passing through small towns and lush landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in La Fortuna / Arenal area. Check into a mid-range lodge near the volcano with views of Arenal (pre-book separately or arrange through your travel agent, as this is a different region from the resort). After settling in, visit the famous La Fortuna Waterfall – a 70-meter cascade through rainforest. Swim in the natural pool at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Explore La Fortuna town – a charming, lively hub with restaurants, souvenir shops, and tour operators. Enjoy dinner in town and plan tomorrow's activities.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside soda en route to Arenal – try a fresh fruit batido (smoothie) and a casado. Budget $8–12 USD
meals.dinner: Dinner in La Fortuna town at a mid-range restaurant – Rancho La Cascada or Don Rufino are popular choices. Budget $18–28 USD per person. Try the heart of palm salad and grilled chicken

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your shuttle or rental car transfer to Arenal in advance. The drive offers beautiful scenery but can be long – start early. La Fortuna Waterfall requires a steep staircase descent (and ascent), so wear good shoes and bring water. Entrance fee is approximately $18 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges Nature Walk – Trek through primary rainforest on a spectacular network of hanging bridges suspended high above the forest floor, with stunning views of Arenal Volcano on clear mornings. A naturalist guide will help you spot poison dart frogs, toucans, howler monkeys, and countless tropical plants. The misty early morning is the best time for wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hanging bridges walk, head to one of Arenal's famous natural hot springs. Tabacón Grand Spa Thermal Resort or Baldi Hot Springs offer mid-range access to volcanic thermal pools surrounded by lush gardens – the perfect way to soothe muscles after the morning hike.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the hot springs into the early evening (many are lit beautifully at night). Return to your lodge for dinner at an on-site or nearby restaurant with volcano views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Arenal lodge – typically included with mid-range accommodations
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hanging bridges visitor center café, or pack snacks from town. Budget $10–15 USD
meals.dinner: Dinner at your lodge or a nearby restaurant with Arenal Volcano views – budget $20–28 USD per person. Try a hearty beef stew (olla de carne) or fresh tilapia

day_by_day.notes: Book the hanging bridges tour in advance – the Mistico Arenal Hanging Bridges Park is highly recommended. Hot springs admission typically ranges from $30–60 USD depending on the resort; Baldi is more budget-friendly, while Tabacón is more luxurious. Check if your lodge offers a hot springs package deal.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart Arenal region early for the journey to Monteverde Cloud Forest (approximately 3–4 hours, partially on unpaved mountain roads). The winding road through the mountains is an adventure in itself, with breathtaking highland scenery. Arrive in Monteverde/Santa Elena and check into your mid-range cloud forest lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a self-guided walk through the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve – a quieter, slightly more affordable alternative to the main Monteverde reserve. Explore misty forest trails, spot quetzals (if lucky), hummingbirds, and exotic orchids.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Santa Elena town – a charming mountain village with artisan shops, local restaurants, and a relaxed vibe. Visit a local cheese factory (Monteverde is famous for its dairy products) and pick up some artisan cheese for snacking.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Arenal lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Santa Elena town upon arrival – try Morpho's Restaurant, a beloved local spot. Budget $10–15 USD. Recommended: vegetable soup and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Santa Elena – Tree House Restaurant & Bar is a unique option built around a 100-year-old fig tree. Budget $18–25 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: The road to Monteverde is notoriously bumpy – a 4WD vehicle is strongly recommended, or take a shared shuttle for comfort. Bring a light jacket and layers as Monteverde is significantly cooler and mistier than the coast. The cloud forest environment is magical but can be chilly at night.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour – The highlight of the trip! Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic and thrilling zip-line circuits. The Original Canopy Tour or Sky Adventures Monteverde offer world-class zip-line experiences with cables stretching hundreds of meters through the cloud forest. Feel the rush as you fly above the treetops with panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and/or the Hummingbird Gallery near the main cloud forest reserve. These compact but fascinating attractions offer close-up encounters with hundreds of butterfly species and dozens of hummingbird species feeding at garden stations – a wildlife photographer's dream.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a night walk in the Monteverde Cloud Forest with a naturalist guide. After dark, the forest comes alive with kinkajous, glass frogs, tarantulas, stick insects, and sleeping birds. This is one of the most memorable wildlife experiences in Costa Rica.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your cloud forest lodge – enjoy local eggs, fresh cheese, and strong Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a café near the zip-line or butterfly garden – budget $10–14 USD. Try a fresh empanada and tropical fruit plate
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sabor Tico, a local family restaurant in Santa Elena serving authentic Costa Rican home cooking. Budget $12–18 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the zip-line tour in advance as spots fill up quickly, especially in high season (February is peak season). Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable clothes you don't mind getting dirty. The night walk requires advance booking and usually costs $25–35 USD per person. Bring a headlamp or flashlight.

day_by_day.morning: Guided morning walk through the main Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve with a certified naturalist guide. This UNESCO-recognized reserve protects one of the world's most important cloud forests. Your guide will help you identify the elusive resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbirds, and hundreds of orchid species. The morning mist creates an ethereal, magical atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: Depart Monteverde after lunch for the journey to Tortuguero on the Caribbean coast (approximately 5–6 hours including a boat transfer). This is a longer travel day but the journey itself is part of the adventure, ending with a scenic boat ride through jungle canals to reach Tortuguero – a town accessible only by boat or small plane.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Tortuguero and check into a mid-range eco-lodge within or near the national park. Enjoy a welcome dinner at the lodge and a briefing from your guide about tomorrow's wildlife boat safari. Rest up for an early start.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Monteverde lodge before the forest walk
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Santa Elena before departing for Tortuguero – grab a sandwich and fresh juice from a local bakery. Budget $8–12 USD
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at your Tortuguero eco-lodge – typically included in lodge packages. Enjoy Caribbean-style rice and beans (cooked in coconut milk), jerk chicken, and fresh plantains

day_by_day.notes: The Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve entrance fee is approximately $25 USD. Guided tours cost extra but are highly worthwhile. The Tortuguero transfer typically departs from Cariari or Guápiles – confirm logistics with your tour operator. February is a good time for Tortuguero as green sea turtles may still be nesting.

day_by_day.morning: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari – Glide silently through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided motorized boat safari at dawn, when wildlife activity is at its peak. Spot caimans basking on riverbanks, river otters, Jesus Christ lizards running across the water, poison dart frogs, manatees (if lucky), howler monkeys, and an extraordinary variety of tropical birds including kingfishers, herons, and toucans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Tortuguero village on foot – a tiny, colorful Caribbean community with no roads, only footpaths and canals. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center to learn about the vital conservation work protecting nesting leatherback and green sea turtles. Take a kayak tour through smaller canals for a more intimate wildlife experience.
day_by_day.evening: If timing and season align, join a guided nighttime sea turtle nesting observation tour on Tortuguero beach (February may catch the tail end of leatherback season). This is a once-in-a-lifetime wildlife experience conducted under strict conservation guidelines. Return to the lodge for dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast at the lodge before the dawn boat safari (usually 5:30–6:00 AM departure)
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge or at Miss Junies, a beloved local Caribbean restaurant in Tortuguero village. Budget $10–15 USD. Must-try: rice and beans Caribbean style with fresh fish
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge – Caribbean cuisine with fresh catch, coconut-based dishes, and tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: The boat safari is best done at dawn and dusk for maximum wildlife activity. Bring binoculars, a good camera with zoom lens, and insect repellent. Turtle tours are strictly regulated – only go with licensed guides and follow all conservation rules (no flash photography, quiet voices). Check with your lodge about turtle tour availability in February.

day_by_day.morning: Second early morning wildlife boat safari through different canal routes in Tortuguero, exploring deeper into the national park. Your guide will take you to areas with higher concentrations of caimans, river turtles, and exotic birds. Spend time birding along the canal banks – Tortuguero is a world-class birding destination with over 300 species recorded.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day: Depart Tortuguero by boat and connecting transfer back toward San José or toward the Pacific coast to return to Aegean Bliss Resort. This is another scenic travel day through Costa Rica's diverse landscapes. Arrive back at the resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome back to Aegean Bliss Resort! Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort restaurant to celebrate the end of the inland adventure circuit. Reflect on the incredible wildlife and landscapes experienced over the past week.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Tortuguero lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch en route – stop at a roadside soda or restaurant during the transfer. Budget $10–15 USD
meals.dinner: Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant – treat yourself to a slightly more indulgent meal to celebrate. Budget $25–35 USD per person. Try the grilled lobster or surf-and-turf if available

day_by_day.notes: The return journey from Tortuguero involves a boat transfer to the mainland followed by a bus or shuttle – confirm all logistics with your tour operator. Journey time is approximately 4–5 hours total. It's a long travel day so rest is important for the final days of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a slow breakfast on the terrace, then take a guided snorkeling or stand-up paddleboard tour along the coastline near the resort. The Pacific coast offers excellent marine life including tropical fish, rays, and sea turtles near rocky outcroppings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day boat tour to explore nearby coastal wildlife – look for dolphins (bottlenose and spinner dolphins are common), humpback whales (February is within whale season!), and seabirds. Many local operators offer combination whale-watching and snorkeling tours from the resort area.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach walk followed by a farewell-style dinner at one of the best restaurants in the resort area. Splurge slightly for a memorable final full-day evening meal with ocean views, celebrating an incredible 13-day journey through Costa Rica.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast – enjoy every tropical fruit and local specialty on offer
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside café or resort pool bar – ceviche, fresh coconut water, and tropical fruit. Budget $12–18 USD
meals.dinner: Special dinner at a top-rated local restaurant – budget $30–40 USD per person. Try whole grilled snapper, shrimp in tamarind sauce, and a local dessert like tres leches cake

day_by_day.notes: February is within humpback whale season on the Pacific coast – whale sightings are quite likely. Book the boat tour the night before to secure spots. Apply reef-safe sunscreen for all water activities to protect Costa Rica's marine ecosystems. This is a great day for souvenir shopping in the resort area.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Wake up early one last time for a sunrise beach walk – soak in the colors of the Pacific dawn and reflect on 13 days of extraordinary eco-adventures, wildlife encounters, and cultural experiences. Pack, check out, and arrange your transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, you may have time to stop in San José for a quick visit to the Mercado Central (Central Market) for last-minute souvenirs – local coffee, chocolate, hot sauce, and artisan crafts make excellent gifts. Arrive at the airport with plenty of time for international check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departure flight home, carrying memories of cloud forests, volcanic landscapes, Caribbean canals, Pacific beaches, and an extraordinary wealth of Costa Rican wildlife. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – savor every bite of gallo pinto and fresh tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at San José's Mercado Central if time allows – try a traditional soup (sopa negra or olla de carne) for $5–8 USD, or grab airport food if pressed for time
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international flight for check-in, security, and immigration at Juan Santamaría Airport. Pre-book your resort-to-airport transfer. Costa Rican customs allows you to bring home up to $500 USD worth of goods duty-free. Don't forget to pick up locally grown Costa Rican coffee – it's among the world's finest. Exit tax is typically included in international airfare but confirm with your airline.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and suspension bridges, this tour offers breathtaking aerial views of the forest and chances to spot toucans, howler monkeys, and resplendent quetzals along the way.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and over 300 bird species. Between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges Nature Walk
experiences.description: Trek through primary rainforest on a network of hanging bridges suspended high above the forest floor near the iconic Arenal Volcano. This self-guided or guided eco-walk offers stunning volcano views and excellent wildlife spotting opportunities including poison dart frogs, coatis, and exotic birds.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Explore one of Costa Rica's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide armed with a high-powered spotting scope. Encounter white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and basilisk lizards, then cool off on the park's pristine white-sand beaches after the hike.

experiences.name: Traditional Costa Rican Cooking Class & Farm Visit
experiences.description: Visit a local family-run finca (farm) to learn how to prepare authentic Costa Rican dishes including gallo pinto, casado, and fresh ceviche using ingredients harvested directly from the garden. Gain insight into the Pura Vida food culture, enjoy a communal meal, and take home handwritten recipes as a souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer with chilled welcome drinks and a personal concierge will whisk you directly to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a complimentary welcome amenity (local rum cocktail and tropical fruit platter) prepared by the resort.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight
meals.dinner: Late-night light bites from the resort's 24-hour in-room dining menu – recommended: Gallo Pinto fritters, ceviche, and a local Imperial beer or Guaro Sour cocktail

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer pre-arranged. Ensure passports and tourist cards are ready. Costa Rica requires no visa for most nationalities. Resort check-in is available 24/7 for VIP arrivals. Keep the first full day light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort morning – enjoy a gourmet breakfast overlooking the beachfront. Take a guided orientation walk of the resort's private nature trails with the resident naturalist to spot toucans, scarlet macaws, and howler monkeys in the surrounding canopy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private beachfront excursion: snorkeling or kayaking in the crystal-clear waters near the resort. Alternatively, enjoy a poolside session with a signature Costa Rican coffee scrub spa treatment at the resort's luxury wellness center.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar followed by a private candlelit dinner on the beach. Chef's tasting menu featuring locally sourced seafood and Costa Rican fusion cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the resort's main restaurant – tropical fruit, eggs Benedict with plantain, fresh-pressed juices, and Costa Rican shade-grown coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch – grilled mahi-mahi tacos, fresh ceviche, and a coconut agua fresca
meals.dinner: Private beachfront candlelit dinner – 5-course tasting menu with lobster, sea bass, and local produce; wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. No strenuous activities scheduled. Confirm all upcoming excursion bookings with the concierge today. Sunscreen and reef-safe products recommended for all water activities.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private charter vehicle to Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 30–45 minutes depending on resort location). Begin the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike with a certified naturalist guide equipped with high-powered telescopes and binoculars. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and hundreds of bird species in one of Costa Rica's most biodiverse ecosystems.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the hike, enjoy exclusive access to Manuel Antonio's pristine beaches for swimming and relaxation. A private picnic lunch is set up in a shaded beachside area. Explore tide pools and look for marine iguanas and hermit crabs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by private transfer. Freshen up and enjoy dinner at one of the resort's signature restaurants featuring farm-to-table Costa Rican cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the resort before departure – granola, tropical fruits, eggs to order, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet private picnic at Manuel Antonio Beach – artisan sandwiches, fresh tropical fruit, local cheeses, and chilled sparkling water
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant – try the Casado de Lujo (luxury rice and beans plate with grilled tenderloin), hearts of palm salad, and tres leches cake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park limits daily visitor numbers – tickets must be pre-booked. Wear lightweight, moisture-wicking clothing and sturdy walking shoes. Bring insect repellent and reef-safe sunscreen. The park is most active for wildlife in the early morning hours.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Costa Rican Cooking Class & Farm Visit – a private driver takes you to a local family-run finca (farm) where a renowned chef and farm family guide you through harvesting fresh ingredients including plantains, yuca, chayote, and tropical herbs. Learn to prepare Gallo Pinto, Olla de Carne, fresh tortillas, and traditional desserts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the farm experience with a guided coffee and cacao plantation tour. Learn the full bean-to-bar and seed-to-cup process. Enjoy a private tasting session of premium single-origin Costa Rican coffees and artisan chocolates.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort's rooftop lounge with panoramic ocean views, craft cocktails, and live traditional Costa Rican marimba music.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: The dishes you prepare during the cooking class served as a lavish farm-to-table lunch with fresh fruit juices and local craft beer
meals.dinner: Resort rooftop lounge – light tapas-style dinner: plantain chips with guacamole, shrimp skewers, and ceviche; craft cocktails featuring local Guaro spirits

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable clothes you don't mind getting dirty during the farm visit. This is an immersive cultural experience – an excellent opportunity to connect with local traditions. Bring a reusable bag to take home artisan coffee and chocolate purchased directly from the farm.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer to a regional airstrip for a scenic domestic charter flight to Tortuguero (approximately 30–45 minutes by air). Arrive and check in to a premium eco-lodge within or adjacent to Tortuguero National Park. Begin the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari – glide silently through jungle canals on a private canopied boat with an expert naturalist guide. Spot caimans, river otters, manatees, Jesus Christ lizards, and hundreds of bird species including kingfishers and herons.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark for a guided rainforest walk along Tortuguero's jungle trails. Look for poison dart frogs, howler monkeys, and the elusive green turtle (February is nesting season). Return to the eco-lodge for a private afternoon kayaking session through the narrower secondary canals.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise on the main Tortuguero canal with champagne and local appetizers. Return to the eco-lodge for dinner. If February timing aligns, a guided nighttime sea turtle nesting observation on the beach (subject to official park permits and turtle activity).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Eco-lodge open-air restaurant – fresh river fish, rice and beans, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Eco-lodge signature dinner – Caribbean-style coconut rice with shrimp, jerk chicken, plantain, and fresh passion fruit sorbet; local craft beer or wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is accessible only by air or boat – no roads connect it to the rest of Costa Rica, adding to its wild, remote feel. Pack light for this overnight excursion. Bring rain gear as Tortuguero is one of the wettest regions in Costa Rica. Sea turtle observation is strictly regulated – only certified guides can lead night tours and flash photography is prohibited.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning second Wildlife Boat Safari through Tortuguero's canals at dawn – wildlife activity peaks at sunrise. Look for additional species including tapirs near the water's edge and spectacular flocks of migratory birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tortuguero Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center to learn about ongoing conservation research. Explore the small village of Tortuguero on foot – browse local artisan shops and support community-based tourism initiatives.
day_by_day.evening: Charter flight back to the resort area. Private transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Relax and enjoy a soothing resort spa treatment – recommended: hot stone massage with volcanic mineral oils.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge early breakfast before morning safari – fresh fruit, eggs, and local bread
meals.lunch: Village soda (local restaurant) in Tortuguero – authentic Caribbean rice and beans with chicken or fish, fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Resort fine dining restaurant upon return – grilled Costa Rican beef tenderloin with chimichurri, roasted root vegetables, and a premium Chilean or Argentine Malbec

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return charter flight timing with concierge. Tortuguero's village is small and charming – cash in local colones is useful for small purchases. The Sea Turtle Conservancy welcomes donations to support their vital research programs.

day_by_day.morning: Full resort relaxation morning – sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and take advantage of the resort's premium amenities: infinity pool, private beach cabanas, and beachfront yoga session led by the resort's wellness instructor.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional premium add-on: private sport fishing charter along the Pacific coast (subject to resort arrangement) or a guided stand-up paddleboarding session in calm coastal waters. Alternatively, enjoy a couples' or solo spa afternoon with a full wellness package.
day_by_day.evening: Premium sunset sailing cruise along the coastline on a private catamaran with gourmet canapés, champagne, and a live acoustic guitar soundtrack. Watch for dolphins and sea turtles along the way.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent Sunday brunch at the resort – eggs benedict, smoked salmon, artisan pastries, mimosas, and tropical fruit display
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch – fresh ceviche, grilled octopus, watermelon salad, and a signature tropical cocktail
meals.dinner: Catamaran sunset cruise canapés followed by a full dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant – whole grilled snapper, lobster bisque, and passion fruit panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: This is a designated rest and rejuvenation day before the more adventurous second half of the trip. Use this time to confirm all upcoming excursion logistics with the concierge, particularly the Monteverde and Arenal segments which require longer transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs early for Arenal Volcano area (approximately 3–4 hours by road with a premium SUV and professional driver). Enjoy scenic stops along the way including viewpoints overlooking Lake Arenal. Check in to a premium eco-lodge near Arenal with volcano views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges Nature Walk – trek through primary rainforest on a network of suspended hanging bridges high above the forest floor. A certified naturalist guide identifies wildlife including toucans, morpho butterflies, howler monkeys, and rare orchids. The perspective from the bridges offers unparalleled canopy-level views.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the renowned Tabacón or Baldi premium hot springs – naturally heated volcanic thermal pools surrounded by lush rainforest. Enjoy riverside cocktails and a gourmet dinner at the hot springs resort restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside stop at a premium local restaurant en route to Arenal – traditional Casado plate with fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.dinner: Tabacón Grand Spa Thermal Resort restaurant – volcano-view dining with grilled meats, fresh pasta, and local desserts; wine list available

day_by_day.notes: Arenal Volcano is one of Costa Rica's most iconic landmarks. Cloud cover is common – early mornings typically offer the clearest volcano views. Pack layers as Arenal's higher elevation is cooler than the coast. Hanging bridges walk is moderate difficulty – suitable for most fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk around the eco-lodge grounds and Arenal lava fields with a resident guide. Look for coatis, agoutis, and the vivid red poison dart frog. Optional: sunrise kayaking on Lake Arenal with volcano backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium white-water rafting experience on the Sarapiquí or Balsa River (Class II–III rapids, suitable for all levels) with a top-rated outfitter providing full safety equipment and professional guides. Alternatively, mountain biking through Arenal's lava fields and rainforest trails.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge. Enjoy a private chef's dinner on your lodge terrace or balcony with direct volcano views – a romantic, intimate dining experience with a curated Costa Rican menu and wine pairing.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast – fresh tropical fruits, gallo pinto, eggs, and specialty Arenal-region coffee
meals.lunch: Post-rafting riverside lunch at a local rancho – grilled chicken, rice, beans, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Private in-lodge terrace dinner – 4-course menu: hearts of palm soup, mixed greens salad, grilled local beef or catch of the day, and chocolate volcano cake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Confirm river activity difficulty level with outfitter in advance. Waterproof bags are provided for rafting. Volcano views from the lodge terrace are best at dusk and dawn – set an alarm for sunrise. All Arenal-area activities should be booked through the lodge concierge for premium service and safety assurance.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Arenal to Monteverde Cloud Forest (approximately 2.5–3 hours via scenic mountain road or optional 2-hour Lake Arenal boat crossing + short drive – a spectacular journey). Check in to a premium Monteverde eco-lodge nestled in the cloud forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve on a private guided walk – a quieter, less-visited alternative to the main Monteverde reserve. Spot resplendent quetzals (February is excellent for quetzal sightings during pre-nesting season), emerald toucanets, and rare cloud forest orchids.
day_by_day.evening: Night walk in the cloud forest with an expert naturalist guide using red-light torches to spot nocturnal wildlife: kinkajous, olingo, glass frogs, tarantulas, and sleeping birds. Return for a warm dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Arenal lodge breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium café in Monteverde town – gourmet sandwiches, local cheese and charcuterie board, and artisan Monteverde coffee
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant – cloud forest-inspired menu featuring local trout, wild mushroom risotto, and artisan Monteverde cheese plate; hot chocolate made from local cacao to finish

day_by_day.notes: The Lake Arenal boat crossing option is highly recommended for the scenic experience – confirm with concierge. Monteverde is cooler and mistier than coastal areas – pack a light waterproof jacket and layers. February is one of the best months to spot the resplendent quetzal. Night walks require advance booking and are limited in group size.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour – experience one of Costa Rica's most iconic and thrilling zip-line circuits soaring through the misty cloud forest canopy. The premium circuit includes multiple lines, a Tarzan swing, and sky bridges with breathtaking views over the cloud forest and Gulf of Nicoya on clear days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Orchid Garden – private guided tours of these remarkable biodiversity showcases. Then explore the Monteverde Cheese Factory (Fábrica de Quesos), a cooperative established by Quaker settlers in the 1950s, for a premium tasting of local artisan cheeses.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Monteverde dinner at a top-rated local restaurant. Enjoy a cultural evening with traditional Costa Rican folk music and dance performance arranged by the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast before the zip-line adventure – energy-boosting: eggs, fruit, granola, and strong Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Post-zip-line lunch at a Monteverde restaurant with cloud forest views – gallo pinto, fresh salad, and local fruit smoothies
meals.dinner: Premium Monteverde restaurant – multi-course dinner featuring local trout ceviche, cloud forest mushroom soup, grilled tenderloin with chimichurri, and homemade ice cream with tropical sauces

day_by_day.notes: Zip-line tours operate rain or shine – cloud forest mist actually enhances the atmospheric experience. Weight and health restrictions apply for zip-lining – confirm with operator in advance. The Monteverde Cheese Factory products make excellent premium souvenirs to bring home. Book cultural evening performance in advance through the lodge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Monteverde – optional sunrise birdwatching walk at the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve (the most famous reserve in the area) with a private ornithologist guide. The reserve is home to over 400 bird species. Alternatively, enjoy a peaceful morning at the lodge with spa treatments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer back to the Pacific coast and Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 3–4 hours). Enjoy the scenic drive through the mountains and lowlands. Arrive at the resort in the afternoon for a final beach afternoon – swim, relax in a private cabana, and soak in the last hours of Costa Rican paradise.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell gala dinner at the resort – the chef prepares a personalized 6-course tasting menu celebrating the finest ingredients of Costa Rica's diverse regions. Toast with a premium Costa Rican rum or local sparkling wine.

meals.breakfast: Final Monteverde lodge breakfast – leisurely and indulgent before the transfer
meals.lunch: Scenic stop en route at a premium roadside restaurant – fresh ceviche, grilled fish, and cold Imperial beer
meals.dinner: Resort farewell gala dinner – 6-course personalized tasting menu: amuse-bouche, seafood starter, soup, sorbet palate cleanser, main course (choice of lobster or wagyu beef), and a decadent dessert with petit fours and specialty coffee

day_by_day.notes: Use the transfer journey to reflect on the trip's highlights and purchase any last-minute artisan souvenirs at roadside stops. Confirm departure logistics with the concierge this evening: airport transfer timing, luggage handling, and any duty-free or last-minute needs.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy one last gourmet breakfast on the beachfront terrace. Take a final sunrise walk on the beach, collect shells, and breathe in the Pacific Ocean air. Optional: one final spa treatment or yoga session before checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort. Private luxury transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport with a professional driver. Arrive at the airport with ample time for check-in and duty-free shopping. Browse premium Costa Rican souvenirs: single-origin coffee, artisan chocolate, Bribri indigenous crafts, and local rum.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with extraordinary memories of 13 days of eco-adventure, wildlife encounters, cloud forest zip-lines, volcanic hot springs, and world-class luxury hospitality. ¡Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet resort breakfast – go all out: full tropical spread, eggs to order, pastries, fresh juices, and a final cup of Costa Rican shade-grown coffee
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge dining or a final meal at an upscale airport restaurant – ceviche, empanadas, and a farewell Imperial beer or Guaro cocktail
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international check-in, immigration, and security at Juan Santamaría Airport. Costa Rica's airport has excellent duty-free options for premium coffee, chocolate, and spirits. Ensure all wildlife souvenirs comply with CITES regulations – no live animals, coral, or protected species products. Consider leaving a gratuity for outstanding resort and guide staff as a final gesture of appreciation.

query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami
